headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct shared-channel evidence, but shared-index retrieval and broad egress warrant caution.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed files and uses RAG/web search, while risingwave has no documented input channel to ingest Khoj output. The pair lacks a proven shared bridge, so prompt injection is not directly evidenced. Uncertainty stays low because shared index across clients could expose retrieved content if manually bridged.
conditions: IF an operator copies Khoj-generated text into risingwave-facing prompts or configs, injected instructions can propagate.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, file content can become an instruction channel.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste workflow between outputs and inputs.
Add a provenance label to all retrieved snippets before reuse.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation at the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add allowlisted prompt templates for any bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress, but risingwave is documented with no network egress and no data classes touched. There is no shared workspace or authenticated principal shown, so leakage is not established. The main risk is operator-mediated transfer of sensitive notes into another system.
conditions: IF personal notes from Khoj are exported into risingwave logs or tables, sensitive data may persist outside Khoj.
IF a shared workspace is introduced, both agents could access the same files.
mitigations: Avoid placing personal notes in shared directories.
Review any export path from Khoj before sending data onward.
Keep risingwave isolated from note repositories.
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage segregation.
requires-engineering: implement redaction before any export.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, and risingwave exposes no write or git capabilities in the profile. With no overlapping mutable write surface, a direct capability conflict is not plausible from the documented pair. Uncertainty is low because the missing write surfaces are explicit.
conditions: IF risingwave is later granted filesystem or git write access to the same directory as Khoj, write conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, concurrent updates could race.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared assets.
Do not mount the same writable directory into both agents.
Use external locking if shared state is added.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency controls.
requires-engineering: separate git and database ownership per agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can generate retrieved answers from notes, but risingwave has no documented action-taking authority or input pipeline that treats Khoj output as authoritative. The pair therefore lacks a proven default cascade from generated text into irreversible actions. Risk remains limited to manual reuse of incorrect summaries.
conditions: IF an operator pastes Khoj summaries into risingwave SQL, ETL, or config changes, errors can cascade.
IF risingwave is wrapped in an automation layer that trusts Khoj output, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before using Khoj output downstream.
Mark all Khoj outputs as unverified summaries.
Keep risingwave disconnected from any auto-action pipeline.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before execution.
requires-engineering: log provenance for every reused statement.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents, while risingwave has no documented data classes or residency/compliance claims. That makes a compliance mismatch possible only if regulated data is introduced into Khoj and then moved elsewhere. Because the second agent's compliance posture is undocumented, I cite only Khoj and treat the other side as an uncertainty that raises caution.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in Khoj and exported to another jurisdiction, residency obligations may be implicated.
IF risingwave is used to process the same regulated data class without a documented DPA or retention policy, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Classify data before loading it into Khoj.
Do not export regulated notes without a legal review.
Document retention and deletion for any shared data.
requires-engineering: add jurisdiction-aware routing.
requires-engineering: publish a DPA and retention policy for the pipeline.
